newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican north calls for peso slide to spur exports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican north calls for peso slide to spur exports.

text.p: The government of the rich northern state of Nuevo Leon called on Thursday for a weaker peso to spur exports and stem a slide in Mexico's trade surplus.

"Its time to let our peso slide against the dollar at least in an amount equal to the difference between U.S. and Mexican inflation," state Economic Development Secretary Jorge Arrambide Garza told reporters.
He said the margin of undervaluation of the peso had shrunk from 35 percent in the wake of the December 1994 peso devaluation to around five or six percent.
"We've been losing a lot of competitivity," said the official, whose state is home to many of Mexico's export giants such as cement firm Cemex and glassmaker Vitro.

Excluding oil sales abroad, the country's trade balance has recently slid into deficit, he said. In August, Mexican exports were $7.813 billion, of which $939 million came from oil. Imports were $7.549 billion.
